recommendation: EWMA with lambda=0.94 on close-to-close daily log returns is the recommended vol-forecast input for sizing (not GARCH(1,1), not rolling windows, not the Parkinson range estimator).
evidence: Pooled 1d-ahead QLIKE ranking across F03/F04/F12 printed cells (scripts/opt_sweep/c05.py): GARCH(1,1) MLE 1.496020 (F04, n=3799 subsample 2010-10-11..2026-04-13) is the single best point estimate, but it only ties EWMA .94 on the SAME window (1.504550, gap -0.57%, well inside F04's registered |gap|<2% tie band; F04's own audit found the exact gap optimizer-dependent, -0.69% on independent re-derivation, same sign/band) and buys zero crisis-detection edge: both filters lag the Mar-2020 onset by ~72-74 vol pts (GARCH 72.1 vs EWMA 73.6, F04 c2/c3, both PASS >=20 bar but a 1.5pt difference is immaterial against a 72-94pt error). GARCH also requires annual MLE refits (last-fit alpha=0.091/beta=0.902, persistence=0.994) with the added optimizer-convergence sensitivity noted in F04's audit -- machinery cost with no measurable payoff. EWMA .94 is separately the grid-best among all EWMA/rolling combinations tested on the full n=4297 sample in F03 (1.501643 vs ewma_.90 1.506709, ewma_.97 1.526107, roll_21 1.520021, roll_10 1.572183, roll_63 1.574955), beating roll-21 (the close-close 21d baseline, identically 1.520021 in F12) by 1.21% -- though F03's own registered promotion bar (>=3% vs roll-21) was MISSED, so this is a best-of-grid descriptive finding, not a promoted bar-clearing result. F12 additionally rules out substituting range-based (OHLC) information for the close-close input: Parkinson-21d QLIKE 1.634742 is 7.55% WORSE than close-close-21d 1.520021, a clean registered MISS (bar was Parkinson beating by >=5%) -- adding High/Low range data actively hurts 1d-ahead QLIKE here, contrary to the usual efficiency argument for range estimators. Net ranking (best to worst, all printed numbers): GARCH(1,1) approx= EWMA(.94) [tied, no crisis edge] > EWMA(.90) > roll-21/close-close > EWMA(.97) > roll-10 > roll-63 > Parkinson-21d. Given the tie plus zero crisis-behavior distinction, EWMA .94 is preferred over GARCH on simplicity/robustness grounds (one fixed parameter, no refit/optimizer risk) for a sizing input; F05's existing vol-target sizing design already uses EWMA on this basis, consistent with this adjudication.
confidence: high on the ranking and tie/dominance claims (all numbers reproduce from the cited f03/f04/f12 JSONs and each family's own independent-audit reruns); moderate on the EWMA-over-GARCH preference itself, since it rests on a simplicity/robustness argument layered on top of a statistical tie rather than a printed bar that GARCH failed and EWMA passed -- a design that specifically valued optimizer-refined average-day accuracy over refit simplicity could reasonably pick GARCH(1,1) instead, as the two are genuinely indistinguishable on the registered tie-band test.
